title: feat(pipeline): delete the max generation depth and the depth concept
body:
Deletes the `max` generation depth and the depth concept entirely. **86 files, +788 / −9051.** Fourth of five PRs in the multi-stage pipeline programme, after #990, #991 and #992.

## Why

`max` cost roughly 12+ model calls per run — a section-by-section fan-out plus an `llm_judge` stage whose output was Warning-only model opinion that nothing in the app acted on. That is pure token spend. #992 already cut the apply flow over to the staged quality pipeline unconditionally, so the depth selectors were steering a choice that no longer existed.

The staged pipeline is now the only one: `analyze_job → match_evidence → strategy → draft → cover_letter → validate → repair → humanize`.

## Deleted

**Rust** — `stages/judge.rs`, `stages/section_gen.rs`, `section_prompts.rs`, `max_pipeline()`/`MAX_STAGES`, `regenerate_max_entry`, the section-observer half of the run hooks, `Budget::RESUME_MAX`, `MAX_RUN_FIXED_SECS`, `GenerationDepth` and the request's `depth` field. `types_max.rs` trims to `ProjectOut` and `assemble.rs` to `render_project` — both load-bearing for #990's deterministic projects normalization.

**Renderer** — `DepthSelector`, `SectionTimeline`, `GenerationDepthPreferences`, the `useGenerationDepth` slice, `lib/generate/generation-depth.ts`, and the pipeline machine's per-section fold.

`TailoredResumePanel` survives this PR deliberately — see below.

## Existing user data keeps working

This is where a deletion this size actually fails, so it got the most attention. Three things are deliberately kept as read-only historic vocabulary, because users have runs recorded at all three depths:

- `RunRow.depth` stays a plain column, now always writing `"quality"`. **No migration** — verified correct by executing SQL probes that insert pre-deletion rows on retired stages and exercising the read, snapshot, write and import paths.
- `GENERATION_DEPTHS` in `packages/shared`, so an old `max` row renders "Max" rather than a raw token.
- `pipeline.stage.sections|assemble|llm_judge` translations.

That last one was a **caught regression, not a plan**. The first pass froze the depth vocabulary with a test, then deleted the stage names — which live on the *same rows*, of the *same feature*, rendered by the *same component* one line away. Review caught it by rendering a stored run and seeing three untranslated wire tokens next to a translated one. The fix-round enumeration then found two further render sites, because the live stage label replays from the last persisted event on reconnect.

## Behavior change worth stating

On a **historic `max` run**, regenerating one role (`SectionKey::Experience(n)`) no longer has its per-entry path, so it falls through to `regenerate_one_section` and rewrites the **whole Work Experience section**. The deleted path had guaranteed the opposite. This is inherent to deleting `max` and was already the documented degrade — no code change — but it is user-visible and belongs in the release notes.

## Review

`rust-backend-architect` APPROVE, `frontend-reviewer` BLOCK→resolved. Both ran every gate themselves and mutation-tested each claimed guard rather than reading them. Three findings are worth recording:

**Two functions went dead with zero signal.** An author verified a helper's last consumer and stopped one hop short — that consumer was itself deleted by this PR. Both are `pub` in a `pub` module of a lib crate, so `dead_code` structurally cannot fire; they survived 4175 tests, `clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`, and the architecture suite. Found by deleting them and compiling. Applying the same method one hop further found a **third** (`sections::entry_range`, whose only callers lived in a test file this PR deletes) plus a chain of private helpers.

**A "guard" that only tested itself.** `PIPELINE_RUN_DEPTHS_HISTORIC` had zero production consumers — the component interpolates the label key directly. Truncating the constant reddened only the test's own assertion about the constant. Dropped; the label assertions that do hold were kept.

**The showcase separator lost its only pin.** Changing `PROJECT_SEPARATOR` from `" · "` to `" - "` passed the whole suite, because the deleted `max_test.rs` had held the only verbatim render assertions. That glyph feeds `consistency::tier_of` / `project_entry_starts` on the Projects section, so it is now pinned and mutation-tested.

## Scope note

`TailoredResumePanel` moves to PR-5. The first pass deleted it, then found it also hosts the agentic "Improve this résumé" flow, which nothing in the apply flow ports — so it reverted rather than orphaning a feature shipped six commits earlier. PR-5 already owns `improve_resume`, so the panel dies there alongside it. Here it keeps only the quality run: its depth picker and section timeline are gone, so nothing dead is left behind for a PR.

Also swept: the orphaned `pipeline.section.*` subtree (~17 keys × 2 locales), each verified unreferenced first — given the HIGH above is exactly what happens when a key looks dead and is not.

## Testing

`cargo test --workspace` 4175 passed / 26 ignored + 18 architecture + 3 eval · `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings` clean · `cargo fmt --check` · `gen:ipc:check` + `gen:prompts:check` · `pnpm typecheck` 13/13 · `pnpm test` 485 files / 7118 tests · `pnpm lint:strict --max-warnings 0` · en/de parity, zero orphans.

  * Résumé generation now uses a single staged quality workflow.

  * Improved recovery when a run fails before live status updates are available.

  * Updated guidance and translations for the current résumé generation process.
